program.title: Program
program.coreLocked: Tunnel running — stop it to swap the core
program.logEmpty: Nothing in this filter — try another one
app.mask.startHint: The connectivity check takes up to 3 s; if it fails the start is cancelled and the reason shown.
app.mask.startingHint: Probing the upstream proxy and clearing leftover adapters and processes — do not click again.
app.mask.stoppingHint: Waiting for the child process to exit and the adapter to be released — do not click again.
app.close.hint: tun2proxy is a background service: quitting takes the running tunnel with it and your network drops. Minimising to the tray keeps it running.
app.traffic.empty: Once started, the live direct and proxied rates show up here.
app.traffic.emptyHint: No traffic yet — once the tunnel runs, one bar is drawn per second
app.sessionsFull: Session slots are exhausted: new connections are dropped. Raise the session limit on the Profiles page.
network.ipv6Hint: When off only IPv4 is forwarded: IPv6 sites time out first and then fall back, which feels slow.
network.autoRouteHint: When off you have to write the routing rules yourself, otherwise traffic never enters the tunnel.
network.unshareHint: On Linux the tunnel gets its own network namespace; on Windows it does nothing, so leave it off.
network.udpHint: Lets UDP (DNS, games, video calls) go through the upstream proxy; leave the server empty to disable it.
network.bypassHint: One IP or CIDR per line — these go direct, never through the upstream proxy. tun2proxy parses the whole line as an address, so comments are not allowed.
network.editingProfile: Editing “{profile}”. Restart the tunnel to apply; MTU, timeouts and the session limit live under Profiles → Edit.
profiles.savedCount: {count} saved. Click a row to switch — the tunnel starts with the one marked Current.
profiles.virtualPoolFieldHint: The fake range handed out to domain names while DNS is intercepted
profiles.bypassHint: One IP or CIDR per line — these never enter the tunnel
program.windowHint: What the close button does, and which language the interface uses
program.closeHint: tun2proxy is a background service — closing the window by mistake takes the tunnel with it
program.languageHint: System follows the OS language; a change applies immediately
program.trayHint: While the tunnel runs in the background you can tuck the window into the tray and click the icon to bring it back
program.aboutBlurb: A GUI front end for the official tun2proxy binary — Rust backend, nsh interface
program.logEmptyHint: No log yet — core output shows up here once the tunnel starts
program.logPathHint: The full log lives on disk — see the Logs path above.
split.directChinaHint: Domains and IPs on the China lists go out over the local network; everything else still uses the proxy. Restart the tunnel to apply.
split.groupsHint: Toggle per group — a disabled group is not matched and its traffic goes through the proxy.
split.customRulesHint: One per line: qq.com (suffix), full:www.qq.com (exact), keyword:bilili (contains), 203.0.113.0/24 (range), proxy:example.org (force through the proxy). Text after # is a comment.
split.builtinListsHint: The built-in lists expanded rule by rule — a disabled rule no longer goes direct. Restart the tunnel to apply.
split.egressHint: Which adapter direct traffic leaves through, and which DNS resolves it. Leave the adapter empty to pick automatically.
split.directDnsHint: IP only (port 53). Use a domestic resolver so direct sites are not handed overseas nodes.
split.egressAdapterHint: Adapter name or interface index; empty means the routing table decides.
split.recentHint: Newest first — whether the connection went direct or through the proxy, and why.
split.listUpdatesHint: The lists ship with the app; you can also re-fetch them from APNIC and v2fly here. Restart the tunnel to apply.
split.statusHint: Once the tunnel starts, the listen address and active rule count show up here
split.disabledHint: All traffic goes through the upstream proxy, exactly as without this feature
split.dnsModeWarning: The DNS mode is “{mode}”: tun2proxy only sees IPs, so the domain lists do nothing and only IP ranges are split. Switch the DNS mode to “Virtual IP” to use the domain rules.
split.rulesTruncated: Showing the first {rows} — use the search box above to reach later rules
split.status: Listening on {addr}, {rules} rules active · this run: direct {direct} / proxied {proxy} / failed {failed}
dash.route.title: Where traffic goes
dash.route.hint: The last two minutes in 2-second steps: direct at the bottom, proxied above it, failures on top.
dash.route.empty: Once the tunnel starts this shows where each connection went.
dash.route.off: The splitter is not running: no new decisions land here until the tunnel starts.
dash.route.idle: No connection has reached the splitter yet. That is normal while idle.
dash.route.totals: The chart covers the last 2 minutes in 2-second steps; the numbers are this run's totals ({count} connections).
dash.profile.title: Current profile
dash.profile.hint: The tunnel starts with this profile; switching applies on the next start.
dash.profile.empty: This profile has no proxy address yet, so starting will fail; use “Edit” to fill it in.
dash.split.title: Split routing
dash.split.hint: Each connection is classified once: matches go direct, the rest use the upstream proxy.
dash.env.title: Environment
dash.env.hint: The config and the logs live here; check the log directory first.
dash.log.title: Recent log
dash.log.hint: The last 5 lines; the full list and filters are on the Program page.
dash.log.empty: No log yet. The latest lines show up here once the tunnel starts.
